solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Puzzle number 100's turn to be set

indicators.note: to turn something round is to send it back the way it came, so the pair before it read backwards

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
to fuse is to become solid or joined, as molten material does when it sets

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's hundredth crossword comes round, and it is their turn to compile it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses NO + C to give CON; 'number 100' looks like a puzzle number but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to puzzle someone is to bewilder or perplex them.

clue.text: What may get docked, perhaps, cut short

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a dog's tail, which owners sometimes have docked

explanation.surface: Something trimmed back, like a docked tail, is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut back or abridge; split in two it is a mongrel's tail, the thing a vet might dock.

clue.text: Starts to experience routine grind in deadening accounting task

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the deadening word

parts.note: numbing means deadening sensation

indicators.note: the starts of the two words are their initial letters

parts.note: to crunch is to grind or crush noisily

explanation.surface: Starting work on the dull routine of an accountant's mind-numbing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grind' looks like the dull routine, but it supplies the crunching piece; 'deadening' wraps around everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for doing large volumes of calculation, the bread and butter of accountants.

clue.text: Exploitation at the hands of girlfriend at chucking-out time?

parts.note: use is the act of exploiting something
by marks the agent, as in killed by
a date is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A girlfriend being used, until the moment she is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucking-out time' sounds like pub closing, but here it is when food in the fridge must be thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Label on food: after the stated day the product should be binned, so it marks when to throw it out.

clue.text: Follow canal almost to the end after turning north-east

indicators.note: after says the turned compass piece comes before the shortened canal in the answer
turning round means the compass abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: going almost to the end means stopping one letter short

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: Directions: follow the canal nearly to its end once you have turned north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like route directions; the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ensue is to come after or result from something.

clue.text: Blade broke off with girl

parts.note: to cut is to sever or break off
a lass is a girl, especially in northern Britain and Scotland

explanation.surface: A sword snapped, and a young woman was there with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, the kind of blade associated with pirates and sailors.

clue.text: Drunken eructation after putting away fifth liqueur

indicators.note: something drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order
putting away the fifth letter removes it from the word

explanation.surface: A drunken belch after a fifth glass of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting away fifth' takes out the T of ERUCTATION, and 'Drunken' rearranges the rest. Eructation is a formal word for belching.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is an orange-flavoured French liqueur.

clue.text: Count space as something sacred

parts.note: to tot up is to count
an em is a printer's space, the width of the letter M

explanation.surface: Treating counting the space around you as a holy act.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem revered as sacred by a group.

clue.text: Nerd from south, induced by feds to take part in deeds, making more than one confession

indicators.note: taking part in means going into the middle of

parts.note: acts are deeds

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a wonk is a studious nerd
led means induced or persuaded
G-men are FBI agents, the feds

explanation.surface: A geek, coaxed by FBI agents into joining their operations, ends up admitting things.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men is old American slang for FBI agents ('government men'). The reversed nerd reads KNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: An acknowledgment is an admission, so the plural stands for several confessions.

clue.text: Young man scores verses

parts.note: a son is a young man, or a familiar way to address one
to net is to score, as in netting a goal

explanation.surface: A young man scores some poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets are fourteen-line poems, a kind of verse.

clue.text: Legendary spinner in Trump kiss and tell broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper-style story about a kiss-and-tell exposé of Donald Trump being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges IN TRUMP KISS TELL, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grimms' fairy tale the imp spins straw into gold, making him the spinner of legend.

clue.text: Head off thin imitation

indicators.note: taking the head off a word drops its first letter

parts.note: papery means thin like paper

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut the head off something flimsy, presented as a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the first letter of PAPERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is the act of aping, that is mimicking or copying others.

clue.text: Old office worker increasingly striking leader without warning

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: striking out a leader removes the first letter

parts.note: more and more, or 'more', means increasingly

explanation.surface: A former temp grows ever keener to strike against the union leader, without notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking leader' deletes the M of MORE to leave ORE. 'striking' looks like industrial action but is a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore means spoken or done on the spur of the moment, with no preparation or advance notice.

clue.text: Making money, renegade crossword compiler's after endless fortune

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: luck is fortune
a rat is a deserter or turncoat
the setter speaks as I, so 'compiler's' (compiler has) is I'VE

explanation.surface: A rogue crossword setter is chasing endless riches to make cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link here: the renegade and the compiler's piece come after the shortened fortune, which is how the charade reads anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative venture is profitable, one that brings in a lot of cash.

clue.text: Ireland and Italy's old clothes taken in by Red Cross

parts.note: IR is a standard abbreviation for Ireland or Irish

indicators.note: taken in means held inside

parts.note: taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
tat is shabby old stuff, including worn clothing

explanation.surface: Charity shop donations from two countries are collected by the Red Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' looks like the charity, but 'Cross' is the definition and 'Red' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being cross means being annoyed or vexed.

clue.text: Pet drinks milk, perhaps, halving quantity inside

definitions.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, also called the sulks, which is a plural noun

indicators.note: the hundred (C) inside is halved to fifty (L), a Roman numeral swap

parts.note: a baby or young animal sucks milk

explanation.surface: A household pet laps up milk, but only half the usual amount.
explanation.walkthrough: C is Roman 100 and L is 50, so halving the C inside SUCKS gives L. 'Pet' looks like an animal but means a sulky mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pet is to be in a huff, the same as having the sulks.

clue.text: As balls reach slip, spinning

indicators.note: a spinning ball turns, so the letters turn into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: the ball turns as it reaches the slip fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a fielding position beside the wicketkeeper and a spinner makes the ball turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls are round, so spherical describes the shape they have.

clue.text: Stir up disputes in discussion

indicators.note: a discussion is spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: rows (rhyming with cows) are quarrels or disputes

explanation.surface: Arguments that come up during a debate stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rouse is to wake, excite or stir someone up.

clue.text: Bureaucracy became more streamlined, getting bloody towards the top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so the piece moves to the front

parts.note: tapered means narrowed to a streamlined shape
blood is red

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic process gets slimmed down, but becomes bloody near the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the top' shifts the RED at the end of TAPERED to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the excessive official paperwork and rules of bureaucratic systems.

clue.text: Micawber's last Toughie'd to be rewritten — early draft had a hard time

indicators.note: the last letter of the setter's pseudonym is taken
rewritten text is put down again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Micawber's final Toughie needed rewriting, and that early draft went through a rough patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rewritten' rearranges R (from 'last') with TOUGHIED. 'early draft' is a second, joking reading: split differently, the letters also give ROUGH EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to rough it is to put up with hardship, so the past tense describes enduring a tough time.

clue.text: Allowing no exception to count

parts.note: a tally is a count, or to tally is to count

explanation.surface: An insistence that every single one should count, no exceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means wholly or completely, admitting no exceptions.

clue.text: Painted like a warrior?

definitions.meaning: ... with paint, as a room might be
a soldier honoured with medals for bravery

explanation.surface: A face covered in war paint, as a warrior wears it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means adorned with paint and also honoured with a medal, as soldiers are.

clue.text: He told tale about woman succumbing to temptation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in Genesis, Eve gave in to the serpent and ate the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: A man recounts a story about a woman giving in to temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales include The Reeve's Tale, told by an estate manager, the Reeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: the Reeve is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims who tells a tale.

clue.text: Getting up, one's played with bow and arrows

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a Strad, a Stradivarius violin, is played with a bow

explanation.surface: An archer rises, saying that one is played with a bow and arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow and arrows' looks like archery, but the bow belongs to a violin and 'arrows' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts are small arrows, thrown by hand in the pub game.

clue.text: Watch over terms of reference

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a timer is a watch or clock that measures time

explanation.surface: A committee is told to watch over its own terms of reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch over' looks like a phrase meaning guard, but 'over' reverses TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of a body's authority, the brief it has been given to work within.

clue.text: Sparing nothing, American Nato ally bust gut

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
sparing means leaving something out, here the zero

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An American ally in NATO, holding nothing back, has busted a gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparing' removes an O from AMERICAN NATO ALLY, and 'bust' rearranges the fifteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the whole digestive tract, which anatomists also call the gut.

clue.text: Wander round university sector, following example of intellectual

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: round means going around something, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to gad about is to wander in search of pleasure
HE stands for higher education, the university sector

explanation.surface: Someone wanders around campus in the footsteps of a model academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university sector' is HE, higher education, the British term for universities and colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an egghead is a bookish, highbrow person.

clue.text: See rope dropped in catching crabs?

indicators.note: one piece drops into the middle of another

parts.note: to spy is to see or catch sight of
a lashing, or lash, is a rope used to tie things down

explanation.surface: Someone watches a rope go down into the sea to catch crabs.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, to catch a crab is to fumble a stroke so the oar slaps the water, a splashy business; the surface makes it look like fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing jargon: catching crabs means botched strokes that throw water about.
